description:
Find when something can be heard in a video or audio file, or in an edit as it plays, from what you describe in plain words, so you go straight to it instead of listening to it all: laughter, applause, a cough, a door slamming, a phone ringing, a dog barking, music starting, someone typing, a car passing. Name each sound and say what it is; you get back the stretches of time where each one can be heard, with the moment it is clearest.
Use it to:
- Find reactions and moments: where the crew or the audience laughs, where people clap or cheer, a gasp, a scream.
- Find trouble to cut or cover: a cough, a sneeze, a phone going off, a door, a siren, wind on the microphone, a click or a bump.
- Find sound to cut on: a clap, a bang, a hit, the music starting or stopping.

HOW IT WORKS. FlexSED, an open-vocabulary sound detection model (local, on the CPU; about 15 to 20 times faster than real time), listens to every 40 ms of the sound and gives each description the probability that it can be heard there. Describe the sound itself, briefly, as you would caption it ("laughter", "a crowd cheering", "glass breaking"), not the scene or a judgment; it is asked as "The sound of <your words>". Short, common sound names work best; put each sound you want in its own entry, up to 16 a call, all listened for at once.
READING THE RESULT. matches gives, per sound, each run of frames at or above min_probability (default 0.5) with its start, end, peak_seconds and frame (for render.frames; media frames for video, timeline frames for an edit). peaks gives the highest probability each sound reaches, and scores every probability (step_seconds apart), for your own cut-off. A sound whose peak stays well under your cut-off is most likely not there; one hovering near it is worth a listen or a lower cut-off.
Media or an edit: with media_id, times are the file's own seconds; with timeline_id, it listens to the edit's mix as it plays (cuts, gaps, levels and effects included), over from_seconds to until_seconds, and times are timeline seconds, so a match is where that sound now sits in the edit. A source or range with no sound fails with no_audio, naming it.
For the 447 sounds with names (Laughter, Applause, Cough, Speech, Music…) as stored data, media.analyze kind sounds. Long-running: returns a task, or a job_id for job.get.

from_seconds.description: Start listening here (media or timeline seconds). Default 0

min_probability.description: A frame matches a sound when its probability is at least this

sounds.description: Name (yours) to the sound in plain words: what it is, as you would caption it ("laughter", "a crowd cheering", "a door slams", "a phone ringing", "a dog barking", "keyboard typing"). Up to 16, each listened for in every 40 ms frame

step_seconds.description: scores: one value per this many seconds (the highest in each). Default 0.04, every frame, coarser when that would be too many

timeline_id.description: Listen to an edit as it plays (timeline seconds): its mix, with cuts, gaps, levels and effects

name: media.listen

asked.description: Per sound: the words the model was given

end.description: Where it ends, on the same clock

frame.description: peak_seconds as a frame number for render.frames: a media frame (video only), or a timeline frame

peak_seconds.description: The middle of the most likely frame

start.description: Where the run of matching 40 ms frames starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

matches.description: Per sound: runs of 40 ms frames that match, in time order; empty when none do

media_id.description: Media handle from media.import or a create.* tool

peaks.description: Per sound: the highest probability anywhere

scores.description: Every probability, for your own cut-off or arithmetic

start_seconds.description: Where the first value starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

step_seconds.description: Seconds each value covers: 0.04 (every frame) unless asked or too long

values.description: Per sound, the highest probability in each step, 0 to 1

timeline_id.description: Timeline handle; every edit returns a new one

job_id.description: Job handle; the same value is the MCP task id

media_id.description: The media it is making; usable in edits once processing

title: Find sounds by description
